chapter: Stuff Smith, 52nd Street and session work
title: Cole's own trio at the Onyx with Guarnieri and D'Amico
summary: On the CBS staff he led a trio at the Onyx; Sinatra came to listen and punched a man who stood in front of him.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Yeah, mostly, yeah. Of course I worked in the Onyx, there were different groups, Hot Lips Paige, I was there with Hot Lips; then I had a little trio in there, my trio with Hank D'Amico and John Guarnieri. See, then's when I was on staff at CBS.
I met Johnny Guarnieri a couple of years ago in Toronto.
They brought him in to play with the house rhythm section at a place called Bourbon Street which is a club up there, jazz club. He still plays very well. He's doing a lot of things in 5-4.
Yeah, Johnny's a great pianist. Yeah, he can mimic Fats Waller down to the nth degree.
Yeah, really small hands, too, for a piano player.
Yeah, Johnny can play. Johnny's a good piano player. Tell you something about that. See we were on staff up there with Raymond.

Mm hmm. So they wanted a trio in the Onyx. The manager approached me and I took a trio to the Onyx which consisted of Johnny, Hank D'Amico and me. We went in there. Hank was, he wasn't a alcoholic but every

night he'd have to have that little taste. So, he'd run up a tab, so at the end of the week, when I would get the money, Hank's would be minus whatever it was. Mine would be minus maybe $8.00 for the whole week of drinking. Johnny's was the only one where he would get full salary, so we used to laugh about that all the time. So when I got paid I'd give Johnny his envelope, and when with Hank, I'd say wait a minute, Hank, we've got to figure up all these tabs that you have had. But that was a good trio. Frank Sinatra used to come in there and hear us all the time.
Did they used to give you a break on the drinks or charge you full price?

Yeah, yeah, they'd give us a break on the drinks, I just forget what it was to tell the truth. One night Frank Sinatra got in a fight down there listening in on our group. Somebody got up and stood in front of-- I've got that somewhere in one of my scrap books--where he punched some guy in the eye for standing in front of him. He said, Man, I want to listen to Cozy's trio. So that was a great gig there, I worked in there with Billie Holiday, Hot Lips Page.
Mm hmm. Hot Lips Page, Billie.
